description: CaeloTerra uses NASA Earth data to support climate-resilient crop rotation and smarter farming decisions. We are looking for teammates with skills in Python, data science, GIS, agriculture, or AI/ML.
summary: CaeloTerra is a climate-resilient crop rotation decision-support system that helps farmers identify multi-season crop strategies that remain robust when environmental conditions change. The system combines real NASA POWER environmental data with farm conditions, farmer-defined priorities, agronomic evidence, and transparent crop-rotation constraints. It generates feasible three-season rotations and evaluates them under Normal, Dry, and Hot controlled stress scenarios. Instead of selecting the rotation that performs best only under normal conditions, CaeloTerra prioritizes the strongest worst-case performance. The result is an explainable, resilience-first planning tool that shows farmers how and why a rotation was selected while clearly distinguishing comparative decision scores from yield predictions, probabilities, or weather forecasts.
details:
CaeloTerra is a climate-resilient crop rotation decision-support system developed for the Field Shift challenge. It addresses a practical agricultural problem: a crop rotation that performs well under normal conditions may become less resilient when rainfall decreases, temperatures increase, or water becomes more constrained.

The workflow begins with the farmer selecting a farm location and entering field information such as the current crop, soil type, irrigation method, and water availability. CaeloTerra then retrieves real environmental observations from NASA POWER for the selected coordinates. The system combines this environmental context with farmer-defined priorities for Water Conservation, Soil Health, and Climate Resilience.

The MVP evaluates six crops—Wheat, Barley, Maize, Lentil, Chickpea, and Tomato—across three future seasons. It initially considers 216 possible sequences and applies explicit agronomic constraints, including preventing consecutive planting of the same crop or crops from the same botanical family.

Every feasible rotation receives comparative Water Fit, Soil Benefit, and Climate Fit scores. Farmer priorities determine the relative contribution of these components.

CaeloTerra then evaluates each rotation under three conditions: Normal, Dry, and Hot. Dry is a controlled what-if scenario with rainfall reduced by 20%, while Hot increases temperature by 2°C. These scenarios are stress tests, not weather forecasts.

The ranking follows a robustness-first strategy. The Most Robust rotation is the one with the strongest weakest-scenario performance rather than simply the highest Normal-condition score.

The system also includes Scenario Lab, Current Practice Comparison, and Why This Plan, allowing users to inspect NASA context, agronomic constraints, rejected rotations, scoring logic, stress-test behavior, evidence sources, and limitations.

CaeloTerra is implemented using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL JS, OpenFreeMap, and a deterministic TypeScript decision engine. NASA POWER is the active environmental input. An optional NASA GPM IMERG precipitation ingestion pipeline is implemented, but authentic GPM data is not currently loaded and therefore does not affect ranking.

CaeloTerra does not predict crop yield, financial return, or probability of success. It is an explainable decision-support prototype intended to help farmers compare crop-rotation resilience under changing environmental conditions.
